Places to Stay

Where to rest your head after a big day out

Turning a day out into an overnight stay changes everything. No rushing back up the motorway, no worrying about the last train, and you get the bonus of an evening stroll along the seafront or a lazy breakfast before round two. The trick is picking the right kind of stay for your trip and your budget.

Your main options

  • Budget hotels – chains like Premier Inn and Travelodge are reliable, often handy for motorways and town centres, and family rooms can be good value.
  • Boutique and independent hotels – more character, better breakfasts and often great restaurants, ideal for couples and special occasions.
  • Guest houses and B&Bs – the seaside classic, with a cooked breakfast and owners who know every corner of the town.
  • Pub rooms and inns – a bed upstairs, dinner and a pint downstairs, perfect for walkers and countryside trips.
  • Holiday lets and cottages – a whole house or flat for families and groups who want space and a kitchen.
  • Glamping and lodges – shepherd's huts, pods and cabins for a cosy outdoor experience without a tent.

How to choose

Start with location. Staying within walking distance of the seafront, attraction or town centre saves parking headaches and lets you nip back for a rest. Families should check what a "family room" actually means – sometimes it's a sofa bed squeezed in. Couples might pay a bit more for a sea view or a hot tub. If anyone needs step-free access, ask specifically about accessible rooms, lifts and parking, as older seaside guest houses often have narrow stairs and no lift.

Booking tips

  • Book early for peak dates – summer weekends, bank holidays and big events fill fast.
  • Check the cancellation policy – flexible rates cost a bit more but are worth it with unpredictable British weather.
  • Ask about parking – city and seaside hotels often charge or have limited spaces.
  • Look at minimum stays – holiday lets often require two or three nights at weekends.
  • Read recent reviews for honest views on noise, cleanliness and breakfast.
  • Ring direct – some places offer better rates or extras when you book with them.

Need somewhere to stay? Have a browse of the cards above for hotels, guest houses and holiday lets, then visit the town pages to see what's on near your bed for the night.

Choose the base before the booking

A hotel deal only tells you part of the story. Work out where you actually want to spend your time, then look at how the accommodation fits around it. Somewhere close to your main stops can make a weekend much easier, especially when you want to go back out for food or an evening on the seafront.

Read the guide before following an offer. Think about the whole visit: getting there, where the car will go, the room you need and what you can do nearby. If you are travelling with children or somebody with access needs, check those details directly with the place before booking. Then use the destination ideas and food guides to turn the stay into a trip you will actually enjoy.
